video.readability.evidence: [audience·claude] Watching it cold, I can follow the rough story: at 0–3.75s an armored skeleton knight with a skull shield is surrounded by tree creatures. At 4.0–4.5s it is overwhelmed and falls apart into bones. At 5.0–6.5s a cross-shaped gravestone rises from the ground. At 6.75s a red magic circle appears. At 7.0–7.75s the gravestone bursts and a pillar of light comes down. At 8.0–9.5s the skeleton re-forms inside the light as a new armored knight. At 11.0–12.75s it slashes the tree creatures, and from 13.0s on it stands alone. Several key points are unclear, though. (1) Who cast the skill: no caster appears in any frame. The gravestone at 5.0s rises on its own, so I can't tell whether this is the knight's own revive, an ally's spell, or a scripted event. (2) What the skill hit: from 6.75s, when the red circle spreads, until 12.0s, the legs of every tree creature carry a red, glowing, root-like effect. They show no hit reaction and keep standing, so I can't tell whether that red is damage, a slow/root, or just ground lighting. (3) Whether the outcome is clear: the kill happens in only about two frames, 12.25s and 12.5s. Those frames are motion-blurred, and the knight is only shown actually slashing about two of the creatures. At 11.75s there are still at least three creatures in frame, but by 12.75s they have all collapsed or are gone, leaving only red lumps on the ground. It doesn't read whether the slashes killed them, the earlier red effect did, or they simply vanished. The knight's look also changes a lot before and after the revive (0s: skull face with skull shield; 9.0s: bulkier armor, glowing eyes, no shield until it reappears at 11.0s), which makes me pause before calling it the same character. Since I can't say with confidence who used what skill, who it hit, or what the result was, this fails.

The spec calls for 'four ends with thick round ball heads' and lists 'religious ornament' among things to avoid. At this cell size I cannot see ball heads on the four ends. In image 2, cells 3–7, the original is a plain small white cross tombstone with no ring. 3) What does match the original: in image 1, the 6.75s cell shows dark red rising under the tombstone, and the 7.0–7.75s cells show a gold-orange light column with the tombstone breaking apart, then dark red on the treants' legs.
